target_customer: Retail investors and wealth managers and advisors wanting portfolios aligned to personal values, sold direct and as white label technology to financial institutions
problem: Investors wanted portfolios that reflect their values but socially responsible funds were coarse, so OpenInvest built custom indexed portfolios at scale tailored to values.
business_model: Asset management platform charging an advisory fee and licensing values based personalization technology to wealth managers (B2B2C)
product_category: Values based direct indexing and robo advisory

founders.name: Conor Murray
education: MIT, math, computer science, economics and philosophy
founders.background_notes: Born in Ireland per YC bio; eight years at Bridgewater building portfolio construction systems.

founders.name: Phillip Wei
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder of Deliveroo on the YC page.

founders.name: Josh Levin
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in press and in Murray's YC bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Portfolio construction, direct indexing with values screens and custodian integrations are standard fintech engineering with some hard parts in tax and rebalancing at scale.

defensibility.rationale: Values data and portfolio tech were copyable by robo advisors and large asset managers, as Betterment later launched SRI portfolios in 2017; advisor integrations added some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Betterment launched socially responsible portfolios in July 2017 and other robos followed, but J.P. Morgan bought OpenInvest in June 2021 to add ESG personalization.

market_need_then: Growing investor interest in socially responsible investing and values alignment, though 2015 evidence in the sources found is limited to the company mission and later robo advisor responses.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven and transparent; talked about radical transparency and values

branding.brand_signature: Public benefit corporation status and values based personalization
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in impact investing press (ImpactAlpha, TriplePundit, SOCAP); kept its brand as a J.P. Morgan company after the sale.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in impact investing and wealth management circles and kept by J.P. Morgan after acquisition, but no evidence of mass consumer awareness.

pivots.from: Direct to consumer socially responsible robo advisor
pivots.to: Technology and white label platform for wealth managers and advisors
pivots.why: Series A funds were to expand into new customer segments and a larger market; the company later described itself as values based personalization at scale for asset and wealth management

outcome_analysis: OpenInvest rode growing demand for ESG and values based investing, raising about $24M across a 2017 seed, a 2018 Series A and a 2020 A1 round, and shifted from consumers toward wealth managers. J.P. Morgan agreed to acquire it in June 2021 after missing out on a separate direct indexing deal, with terms undisclosed, which is a moderate strategic exit rather than a large outcome.
notes: The 2015 $120K figure and the 2017 seed date come from Seedtable and tech.co only; the 2015 round is unverified and the investor attribution there is assumed from YC participation. Total raised is $23.8M per company press release, aggregators range $20.9M to $34.7M. The A1 date of April 2020 comes from a reprint and is not confirmed. Company website returned 503 at fetch time. Deal terms were not disclosed. No competitor source dated near 2015 was found, so the list is empty; Betterment SRI in 2017 is recorded in takeover risk.
